findings.issue_text: [BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher can never validate the grant shortcut: it slices items[0].substring(3, 5), which spans the last char of the token-type shortcut and the first char of the grant shortcut, while the encoder's layout (sessionType[0-1] + tokenType[2-3] + grant[4-5], verifiable from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId and the round-trip test "trltcc:1234") puts the grant shortcut at substring(4, 6) — and it returns false when the sliced value EQUALS the expected shortcut, inverting the match. All four updated expectations (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) accept any `xxxxxx:<uuid>` token id regardless of grant type, so the PR's only integration-level verification of the new encoded token ids is vacuous; and because the slice composes as <tokenType2ndChar><grant1stChar> it can never equal a built-in shortcut, anyone who fixes the inverted comparison alone leaves the wrong slice and turns every one of those assertions red across the entire OIDC testsuite.

[BUG] The constructor's fourth null-guard duplicates the grantType check — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` validates grantType again instead of rawTokenId — so a null rawTokenId passes construction despite the message claiming otherwise. encodeTokenId then emits `…:null` as a token id instead of failing fast: any future caller constructing AccessTokenContext with a null id (e.g., a decode/re-encode path) ships access tokens whose jti is the literal string "null", and the intended IllegalArgumentException fires on the wrong field (grantType is already guaranteed non-null by the previous line).

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType never reaches the IllegalArgumentException it was written for: before() never calls postInit so factory.sessionFactory is null, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut dereferences sessionFactory on the "ac" cache miss, so the RuntimeException caught at line 81 is a NullPointerException from the null session factory rather than the "Unknown value 'ac' for grant type" validation. The grant-shortcut validation branch in getTokenContextFromTokenId stays untested and the test passes for the wrong reason — a regression that deletes or weakens that IllegalArgumentException keeps the test green, and the lazy-resolution code path is only ever exercised via an accidental NPE.

[BUG] getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires a 6-character prefix (encodedContext.length() != 6 throws IllegalArgumentException) while neither encodeTokenId (lines 113-116, which performs no shortcut-length check) nor the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() contract constrains shortcuts to 2 characters — the javadoc explicitly invites "usually like 3-letters shortcut". A custom grant factory returning a 1- or 3-character shortcut makes this same server issue access-token ids that its own decoder rejects with IllegalArgumentException, breaking every consumer of the decode API once it is wired; all ten built-in grants happen to use 2 chars, so neither the postInit duplicate check nor any test catches the inconsistency.

[ADVISORY] Adding the abstract method getShortcut() to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI without a default implementation breaks every existing out-of-tree OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut() on every loaded grant factory during session-factory startup. An operator upgrading Keycloak with any pre-existing custom grant jar gets an AbstractMethodError thrown inside postInit — a hard boot failure of the entire server rather than one disabled grant — and the extension author gets no transition path (a `default` derived shortcut would avoid the brick).

[ADVISORY] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient; the sibling issuance paths in the same provider (OIDC-to-OIDC subject exchange and external-to-Keycloak exchange) mint access tokens through the same tokenManager.responseBuilder without ever setting the attribute on their client session context. Access tokens from the most common token-exchange flows encode the "na" unknown-grant marker instead of "te", so once decode consumers arrive the grant dimension of the encoded context is wrong for the primary token-exchange use case and exchange tokens are indistinguishable from admin-issued ones.

[ADVISORY] The import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory is added but unused — the only new statement in this file references OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE, and pre-existing code cannot have used an import that did not exist before this diff. The unused import trips the repository's checkstyle UnusedImports gate and misleads readers into expecting a TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT-style constant reference that was evidently dropped.

[ADVISORY] The decode half of the framework ships with no production caller (getTokenContextFromTokenId is referenced only by the unit test), and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() bypasses postInit entirely, hand-assigning grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts instead of running the real registry construction. The startup grant scan, the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException, the (OAuth2GrantTypeFactory) cast, and both lazy-resolution branches (lines 104-117 and 119-135, including the null-sessionFactory dereference proven by the unit test's NPE) execute only on untested paths — a regression in postInit surfaces as a hard startup failure of the whole server with zero signal from this diff's tests, landing on whichever follow-up PR first wires decode into production.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId is doubly broken — the comparison is inverted (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails only when the grant MATCHES) and the slice is wrong (substring(3,5) takes tokenType[1]+grant[0], e.g. 'ta' for 'onrtac', instead of substring(4,6) 'ac') — so for every well-formed encoded token the extracted slice never equals the expected shortcut and the check never fires. All four migrated helpers (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) pass for any 'prefix:uuid' token ID regardless of grant type: a refresh flow emitting 'ac' or an auth-code flow emitting 'dg' sails through, meaning the PR's grant-type encoding has no working acceptance verification anywhere in the diff; substring(3,5) on a shorter prefix additionally throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the matcher.

[ADVISORY] The only test hand-seeds duplicate shortcut maps and never calls postInit or getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, so the production wiring that runs on every token issuance via TokenManager.initToken has zero coverage in the diff. A regression in the derivation path (swapped OFFLINE/ONLINE detection, TRANSIENT check removed, grant fallback dropped) or in postInit's grant registration (a factory shortcut typo) mislabels every newly issued access token ID with no test failing; combined with the vacuous AssertEvents matcher, no test in the diff pins the actual encoded format for any grant — the next engineer changing this code has no safety net.

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes via a NullPointerException, not the behavior under test: because postInit is never called, factory.sessionFactory is null, and getGrantTypeByShortcut's lazy-refresh dereferences it for the unseeded 'ac' shortcut, so the intended unknown-grant IllegalArgumentException branch is never executed and the broad catch (RuntimeException) swallows the NPE. The decode-rejection logic for unknown grant shortcuts (the IllegalArgumentException at DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider line 92) is unverified — replacing it with silent acceptance would still pass this test — and the green test masks that the lazy-refresh path NPEs whenever the factory's wiring is incomplete.

[BUG] The constructor's fourth guard is a copy-paste error — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks grantType a second time, so rawTokenId is never null-checked and the message misattributes a null grantType to rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is silently accepted and flows into DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId's string concatenation, producing 'xxXXgg:null' token IDs for every token in the affected flow, and anyone debugging a null grantType gets an NPE message pointing at the wrong field.

[BUG] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only in exchangeClientToOIDCClient, leaving the sibling external token exchange path (ExternalTokenExchangeProvider, same urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange grant, which also issues tokens via tokenManager.responseBuilder and bypasses OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse) with the attribute never set. Access tokens minted via external/identity-brokered token exchange encode grantType as UNKNOWN ('na') instead of 'te', so the framework's stated purpose — recovering the grant from the token ID — silently fails for that flow, and any downstream consumer distinguishing exchanged tokens by the encoded context gets wrong data.

[ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added as an abstract method with no default implementation and no documented null or length contract, while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit (lines 69-76) unconditionally calls it on every registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory and ConcurrentHashMap.put's the result. Out-of-tree grant factories compiled against the previous interface throw AbstractMethodError during postInit at server startup (boot failure for deployments carrying custom grant jars), and a factory returning null from getShortcut() crashes startup with an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...) — both avoidable with a default method plus a null/length check.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-fails any context prefix whose length is not exactly 6 (i.e., it requires 2-char grant shortcuts) while encodeTokenId performs no shortcut-length validation, and the getShortcut() javadoc added in this diff advertises 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' as acceptable. A third-party grant author following the documented guidance gets tokens that encode successfully but whose IDs always throw IllegalArgumentException('Expected length of 6') on decode — the context is permanently unrecoverable for every token that grant issues, and the failure surfaces far from the mistake that caused it.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId inverts its check — it returns false (no match) when the extracted shortcut equals the expected one — and extracts items[0].substring(3,5), which spans the token-type's second character and the grant's first character, instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4,6). Every expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh and expectAuthReqIdToToken assertion reduces to 'the part after the colon is a UUID': the grant-shortcut comparison is unreachable for all in-tree shortcuts (index 3 is always 't' or 'n' from the token-type enum), so a regression that encodes grant 'na' or the wrong grant into access token IDs passes the entire integration suite, while a correctly written matcher with fixed bounds and fixed polarity would fail every currently green test.

[BUG] The constructor null-checks grantType twice — Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") — so rawTokenId is never validated despite the message claiming it is. A caller passing a null rawTokenId gets no exception; encodeTokenId then string-concatenates it into a token ID ending in the literal 'null' (e.g. 'onrtac:null'), issuing structurally corrupt token IDs instead of failing fast, and anyone debugging sees a 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' message pointing at a check that does not exist.

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes by catching a NullPointerException thrown by the test's own wiring: before() hand-installs a three-entry grantsByShortcuts map and never calls postInit, so sessionFactory is null, the 'ac' lookup misses, and the refresh branch in getGrantTypeByShortcut dereferences the null field. The test asserts nothing about decode behavior — the caught RuntimeException is an NPE, not the intended IllegalArgumentException — and against a production-wired factory 'ac' resolves to authorization_code, getTokenContextFromTokenId('ofrtac:5678') succeeds, and Assert.fail fires, so the test only passes because the factory is deliberately mis-wired and would fail the moment it is initialized properly.

[ADVISORY] The framework fails open on missing grant attribution — grantType defaults silently to 'na' — so the encoded grant type is a hand-wired convention across five separate call sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, TokenManager.validateToken) rather than an invariant the encoder enforces. Any issuance path not hand-annotated — a third-party grant that builds its token response outside OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, or a future token-exchange sub-path of exactly the kind this diff already shows bypassing the base class in StandardTokenExchangeProvider — mints tokens whose ID claims grant 'na' with no log or error, so consumers of the encoded context receive wrong metadata indistinguishable from a genuine unknown; encodeTokenId throws on unknown grant types while this derivation path fails silently, guaranteeing such gaps stay invisible.

[ADVISORY] The diff unconditionally activates context encoding in initToken for every realm and client — no feature flag, config option, or realm/client switch, overridable only by deploying a whole replacement provider — while shipping no production consumer of getTokenContextFromTokenId (it is called only from the unit test), so the entire user-visible effect of this PR is a global jti format change serving future work. Every deployment sees access token jti change from a bare UUID to a prefixed string like 'onrtac:<uuid>' on upgrade with no way to switch it off short of shipping a custom provider jar; clients, audit pipelines, or resource servers that validate or store jti as a UUID (UUID-typed DB columns, format-checked dedup keys) break at upgrade, and a rolling upgrade serves mixed-format token IDs from old and new nodes.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only method wired into production token issuance, containing all the real derivation logic (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE session classification, lightweight-token detection, grant lookup) — is executed by no test in this diff. A regression in session-type classification or grant attribute plumbing corrupts the ID of every access token issued and misattributes context to all downstream consumers, and nothing in the diff would notice: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest hand-builds contexts from hardcoded strings and never touches a ClientSessionContext, and the only integration-level observation of the format (AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId) is dead due to the inverted matcher, leaving the PR's headline production path with zero coverage.

[ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI interface with no default implementation, making every grant factory compiled against the previous interface binary-incompatible. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates all registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances and calls gtf.getShortcut(); a deployment carrying a pre-compiled extension grant throws AbstractMethodError at that call and the server fails to start after upgrading — a hard boot failure with no default method, migration note, or documented shortcut contract for existing grant authors.

[ADVISORY] The getShortcut() javadoc contracts for 'usually like 3-letters' shortcuts while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-rejects any encoded context whose length is not exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) with IllegalArgumentException. A third-party grant author following the interface documentation writes a 3-character shortcut and their grant issues token IDs ('onrABC:id') that the framework's own decoder throws on; the mismatch surfaces only at runtime decode because neither postInit's duplicate check nor anything else validates shortcut length at deployment.

[ADVISORY] The diff deletes the public Context(Context) copy constructor instead of extending it to propagate the new grantType field alongside the thirteen fields it already copies, removing SPI surface not required by the encoding feature. Out-of-tree grant implementations that wrap or decorate the grant Context via the copy constructor stop compiling; adding a single line (this.grantType = context.grantType;) preserves them, so the deletion is gratuitous API removal not traceable to the stated intent and forces extension authors to discover the missing constructor at build time.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut implement provider hot-deployment, a scenario Keycloak does not support — grant factories register at startup and adding one requires a restart — so both branches are unreachable for every startup-deployed grant. Deleting both refresh branches (and the sessionFactory field they alone justify) removes ~15 lines with identical behavior; as-is, the dead paths force the unit test to bypass postInit and hand-wire package-private maps, which is exactly what leaves sessionFactory null and lets testIncorrectGrantType pass on an NPE — the machinery actively degrades the tests that exercise it.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId's grant-type check is doubly broken: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns non-match on EQUALITY (inverted polarity) and reads substring(3,5) instead of the grant shortcut's actual position substring(4,6), so the matcher accepts any encoded token id regardless of grant type. The only integration-level verification of the new encoded token ids is vacuous: expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken reduce to 'two colon-separated parts, second is a UUID' — for the shortcuts ac/rt/dg/ci substring(3,5) can never equal the expected value (it spans tokenType[1]+grantType[0], which never starts with 'a','r','d','c'), so a regression that encodes the wrong or 'na' grant type into every access token still ships green; additionally short prefixes like 'ab:uuid' throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside matchesSafely instead of reporting a mismatch.

[BUG] The constructor's rawTokenId null check validates the wrong variable — it calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId passes the guard that was written specifically to reject it, and encodeTokenId then string-concatenates it, silently minting a token id ending in the literal text 'null' (e.g. 'onrtna:null') which round-trips through getTokenContextFromTokenId as rawTokenId "null" instead of failing fast.

[BUG] getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory as a non-default abstract method, so every existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation compiled against the previous interface no longer satisfies the contract. When DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates grant factories at startup and calls gtf.getShortcut(), a deployment containing any pre-upgrade custom grant JAR throws AbstractMethodError and the server fails to start — hard-breaking exactly the third-party grants that the factory's own 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' lazy paths claim to tolerate; a default method would have avoided the break.

[BUG] encodeTokenId concatenates factory.getShortcut() with no length validation while getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-rejects any encoded context whose length != 6, and the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut javadoc explicitly blesses '3-letters' shortcuts. A third-party grant following the interface javadoc with a 3-char shortcut mints access tokens whose ids its own framework decoder throws IllegalArgumentException on ('Expected length of 6'), a write/read format drift invisible to every test because all in-tree shortcuts happen to be 2 chars.

[BUG] The 'pg' shortcut is registered for the UMA grant, but no code path in the UMA permission flow ever sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on its client session context — PermissionGrantType builds its token response directly through tokenManager.responseBuilder rather than OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, and the diff wires none of its sites. Every UMA-ticket access token encodes grant 'na' (or a stale 'grant_type' note left on a reused client session by an earlier grant), so 'pg' is dead vocabulary that is never emitted and UMA tokens are indistinguishable from legacy pre-upgrade tokens to any consumer decoding the id.

[BUG] The public copy constructor Context(Context) is deleted from the OAuth2GrantType extension surface, a binary-incompatible removal from the same SPI this framework extends. Any extension grant that clones a Context via 'new Context(other)' — the pattern the constructor existed to support — dies with NoSuchMethodError after upgrade, with no deprecation cycle; source-level implementers get an unexplained compile break alongside the new getShortcut() requirement.

[BUG] Grant-type wiring covers only StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient; the sibling external-to-internal exchange provider mints OIDC access tokens through the same TokenManager.initToken with nobody setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE. Access tokens minted via external token exchange encode grant 'na' instead of the registered 'te' shortcut, so the framework's grant data is wrong for that entire flow and a decoding consumer cannot tell externally-exchanged tokens from legacy ones.

[ADVISORY] Every access token's public jti claim (and event detail Details.TOKEN_ID) changes from a bare UUID to a fixed-width 'xxxyyyzz:uuid' encoding with no version marker, no config to disable it, and zero production consumers of the decode half (getTokenContextFromTokenId is called only by the unit test). Downstream systems that treated jti/TOKEN_ID as UUIDs — an assumption Keycloak's own codebase demonstrably held, since the diff must rewrite four isUUID() matchers in AssertEvents — break silently on upgrade, and operators take that compat risk immediately for a capability nothing reads until a later PR; the rigid positional format also means any future vocabulary change is a hard decode failure rather than a graceful UNKNOWN fallback.

[ADVISORY] Context eagerly captures grantType as formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE) in the constructor while the adjacent setFormParams mutator replaces formParams without recomputing it, so the two fields can disagree. Any grant implementation that swaps form params after construction — the mutator's entire purpose — mints tokens whose encoded grant type reflects the pre-swap params while context.getFormParams() reports the new ones, producing a silently wrong jti with no inconsistency signal.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId never verifies the encoded grant type: it slices the wrong characters (items[0].substring(3,5) instead of the grant shortcut at chars 4-5, i.e. substring(4,6)) and inverts the comparison by returning false when the slice EQUALS the expected shortcut. With the current enum values the slice can never equal any expected shortcut, so all four rewritten assertions (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) accept any 'xxxxxx:<uuid>'-shaped token ID regardless of which grant was encoded — a regression that encodes the wrong grant type passes CI — and once anyone fixes the slice alone, every valid token starts failing the matcher; the matcher also throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for any prefix shorter than 5 chars, erroring the test run instead of asserting.

[BUG] The constructor's null-guard intended for rawTokenId actually checks grantType a second time (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") at line 71), so rawTokenId is never validated despite the guard's message. A null rawTokenId passes construction and encodeTokenId emits a jti ending in ':null' — the fail-fast contract the error message advertises does not exist, and any caller relying on the constructor's non-null guarantee silently gets corrupted token IDs instead of an NPE at the construction site.

[ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI as an abstract method with no default implementation, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut() on every registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory during Keycloak startup (factory lines ~69-74). Any operator with a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory deployed as a JAR compiled against the previous interface gets AbstractMethodError during server startup (or an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put if a factory returns a null shortcut), turning a token-ID formatting feature into an unbootable server instead of a degraded feature; a default method returning the id-derived or UNKNOWN shortcut would preserve boot.

[ADVISORY] initToken unconditionally rewrites every access token's jti from a plain UUID to a prefixed form (e.g. 'onrtac:<uuid>') via the default TokenContextEncoderProvider, with no feature flag, profile gate, or realm/client option to disable the new format. Every deployment's public token format and every Details.TOKEN_ID event payload change on upgrade with no opt-out short of a code revert — the diff itself had to rewrite four AssertEvents assertions from isUUID() to the new matcher, proving external observable surfaces (SIEM/event pipelines, client tooling that validated token_id/jti as a UUID) change silently; operators cannot roll this back per realm.

[BUG] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only on the exchangeClientToOIDCClient path, so access tokens minted on the sibling user-token exchange path (subject_token=JWT, e.g. exchangeOIDCtoOIDC in the same class) are created with the attribute unset and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes grant type 'na' for them. Tokens from the primary token-exchange flow carry UNKNOWN grant context in their jti while client-to-client exchange tokens carry 'te' — the framework misreports exactly the flows it was built to label, so any consumer keying decisions off the encoded grant treats user-token exchanges as unknown, and the inconsistent labeling defeats round-trip analysis of exchange tokens.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only production-facing method the new TokenManager.initToken path depends on, containing the TRANSIENT/offline/online classification, lightweight-token detection, and missing-grant defaulting — is exercised by no test in the diff (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest only round-trips getTokenContextFromTokenId/encodeTokenId). A regression in the classification (e.g., inverting isOffline so offline tokens encode 'on', or mis-reading the lightweight-token flag) ships green because nothing asserts what prefix a real client session context produces, and the only integration-level check (AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId) is itself non-functional — so every access token realm-wide could be silently encoded with the wrong session or token type.

[ADVISORY] The postInit duplicate-shortcut validation enforces grantsByShortcuts.size() == grantsToShortcuts.size() over all factories in the provider stream, which also fires for the legitimate Keycloak override pattern of two factories sharing one provider id (custom grant replacing a built-in with the same id and a different shortcut). An operator deploying a custom grant that overrides a built-in grant via the standard same-id mechanism gets an IllegalStateException ('Different lengths of maps...') during startup and an unbootable server, with an error message that misdiagnoses a supported override as a configuration mistake.

[BUG] The fourth null-guard in the AccessTokenContext constructor passes grantType instead of rawTokenId (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")), so the constructor accepts a null rawTokenId despite the guard claiming to reject it. Any caller constructing the context with a missing rawTokenId gets no fail-fast; encodeTokenId then string-concatenates the null into the ID, minting token IDs whose raw-ID segment is the literal string "null" (e.g. "onrtac:null"), which getTokenContextFromTokenId happily accepts as a token whose ID is "null" — silently shipping structurally broken IDs exactly where the validation was written to prevent them.

[ADVISORY] Adding getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory as an abstract method with no default implementation breaks binary compatibility with every OAuth2GrantTypeFactory already deployed as a compiled JAR, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit invokes getShortcut() on every registered grant factory at startup. Operators running realms that use any third-party/custom grant SPI implementation compiled against the previous interface get a complete Keycloak startup outage after upgrading: postInit's gtf.getShortcut() throws AbstractMethodError, deployment fails before any traffic is served, and there is no configuration switch to skip unknown factories — the only recourse is patching the extension's source.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires the encoded context to be exactly 6 chars (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise, while the getShortcut() contract in OAuth2GrantTypeFactory explicitly invites "usually like 3-letters shortcut" values and encodeTokenId performs no length validation on the shortcut it concatenates. An extension grant author who follows the documented 3-letter example (or returns any non-2-char shortcut) has tokens minted by encodeTokenId with a 5- or 7-char context that the decoder rejects with "Expected length of 6" for every token that grant ever issues; the invariant is enforced only on the read side, so once getTokenContextFromTokenId is wired into token verification/introspection (the PR's stated purpose) all of that grant's tokens fail processing, far from the misconfiguration that caused it.

[ADVISORY] initToken silently changes the public jti claim of every issued access token from a bare UUID to a prefixed string like "onltac:<uuid>" with no feature flag, config option, or migration path to retain the old format. Downstream resource servers, audit pipelines, and idempotency/dedup stores that treat Keycloak's jti as a UUID (UUID-typed database columns, UUID.fromString parsing, regex matchers on Details.TOKEN_ID events) break for every newly issued token immediately after the upgrade, and because the format change is unconditional it cannot be staged or rolled back per client.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId's grant check is doubly broken: it returns false when the slice EQUALS the expected shortcut (inverted comparison), and it slices items[0].substring(3, 5) — the tokenType's second char plus grantType's first char, e.g. "ta" for "onrtac:<uuid>" — instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4, 6), so the comparison never discriminates anything. All four updated helpers (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) accept any token ID of the form '<6-char prefix>:<uuid>' regardless of encoded grant — e.g. a code-grant token encoding 'na' (GRANT_TYPE attribute never set) or 'ro' passes isAccessTokenId("ac") — so the diff's only end-to-end assertion of the new token-ID format is vacuous and a wrong grant-type wiring ships with a green suite; conversely, fixing only the index without the inverted comparison makes the matcher reject every correctly encoded token and fails the suite.

[BUG] testIncorrectGrantType passes via a NullPointerException thrown by the fixture, not via the validation it claims to test: shortcut 'ac' misses the hand-seeded grantsByShortcuts map, getGrantTypeByShortcut's refresh branch then dereferences the null sessionFactory (postInit is never called in before()), and catch(RuntimeException) swallows that NPE as a pass. The IllegalArgumentException branch for unknown grant shortcuts in getTokenContextFromTokenId — and its sibling unknown-session-type, unknown-token-type, and wrong-length branches, none tested — can be deleted entirely without this test failing; moreover the test's premise is wrong against the real registry, where 'ac' is AuthorizationCodeGrantTypeFactory's legitimate shortcut, so a realistic fixture would make decode succeed and Assert.fail fire — the test verifies the fixture, not the code, and never asserts the exception type or message.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the encode-side entry that TokenManager.initToken calls on every token issuance, containing the TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE session-type selection, the lightweight-token switch, and the grant-null-to-'na' fallback — is executed by no test in this diff (checked services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java, which never references it and builds the provider with a null KeycloakSession, and testsuite/.../AssertEvents.java, whose matcher inspects only the grant characters, and brokenly so). An inverted isOffline()/persistence-state check or a transposed session/token-type shortcut mis-encodes the jti of every access token the server issues while the entire suite stays green; clients and any consumer decoding the ID (the PR's stated purpose) silently receive wrong session-type/token-type values.

[ADVISORY] postInit — the production registration that populates the grant-shortcut maps from deployed OAuth2GrantTypeFactory providers, seeds the UNKNOWN entry, and enforces the duplicate-shortcut IllegalStateException — is never executed by any test; DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before() bypasses it by directly assigning the package-private grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts fields with hand-seeded 'ro'/'cc'/'na' entries. The maps the server actually uses at runtime are never the ones under test: a typo in any *GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() constant, a missing UNKNOWN seed, or a wrong duplicate-shortcut check (which either halts server startup for all realms or silently admits colliding shortcuts that corrupt token-ID decoding) passes the whole suite.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut — including their sessionFactory lookups and map mutations — are executed by no test and are untestable under the current fixture, whose null sessionFactory makes the first dereference NPE (exactly what happens inside testIncorrectGrantType). A regression in hot-deploy shortcut registration (e.g., swapped key/value arguments in the map puts) ships undetected and surfaces only in production as IllegalStateException('Cannot encode token with unknown grantType') on encode or IllegalArgumentException on decode for any grant type deployed after startup.

[BUG] The constructor's fourth null-guard re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId — Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") is a copy-paste of the preceding line — so the intended rawTokenId fail-fast is dead code. An AccessTokenContext built with a null rawTokenId (e.g., by a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider implementation or a future call site) constructs successfully and encodeTokenId then emits a token ID ending in the literal string 'null', breaking JTI uniqueness for every token from that path instead of failing fast as the author intended.

[ADVISORY] The getShortcut() javadoc invites 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' values, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-requires exactly two grant-shortcut chars (encodedContext.length() == 6, substring(4, 6)) and postInit validates only duplicate shortcuts, not their length — encode and decode are asymmetric for any shortcut whose length is not 2. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId inverts its check — it returns false (no match) when the extracted shortcut equals the expected one — and extracts items[0].substring(3,5), which spans the token-type's second character and the grant's first character, instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4,6). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The framework fails open on missing grant attribution — grantType defaults silently to 'na' — so the encoded grant type is a hand-wired convention across five separate call sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, TokenManager.validateToken) rather than an invariant the encoder enforces. Any issuance path not hand-annotated — a third-party grant that builds its token response outside OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, or a future token-exchange sub-path of exactly the kind this diff already shows bypassing the base class in StandardTokenExchangeProvider — mints tokens whose ID claims grant 'na' with no log or error, so consumers of the encoded context receive wrong metadata indistinguishable from a genuine unknown; encodeTokenId throws on unknown grant types while this derivation path fails silently, guaranteeing such gaps stay invisible.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows grant type is propagated into the token-id context only via manually setting `clientSessionCtx`/`sessionContext` attribute `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` in several issuance paths (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`, `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process`, `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process`, `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient`, `TokenManager.validateToken`). In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`, missing attribution silently defaults to `UNKNOWN`/`"na"` rather than enforcing presence or logging. This means any token-issuance path that does not set the attribute will encode a token id with `na` grant metadata, making the metadata unreliable for such paths. However, the finding’s claim that `encodeTokenId` will throw in this scenario is not supported by the diff because the factory explicitly maps `"na"` to itself in `postInit`, so encoding still succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff unconditionally activates context encoding in initToken for every realm and client — no feature flag, config option, or realm/client switch, overridable only by deploying a whole replacement provider — while shipping no production consumer of getTokenContextFromTokenId (it is called only from the unit test), so the entire user-visible effect of this PR is a global jti format change serving future work. Every deployment sees access token jti change from a bare UUID to a prefixed string like 'onrtac:<uuid>' on upgrade with no way to switch it off short of shipping a custom provider jar; clients, audit pipelines, or resource servers that validate or store jti as a UUID (UUID-typed DB columns, format-checked dedup keys) break at upgrade, and a rolling upgrade serves mixed-format token IDs from old and new nodes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token `jti` generation unconditionally in `TokenManager.initToken()` from `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` to `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java), and registers a default internal SPI/provider via `META-INF/services` so this applies globally by default. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the only method wired into production token issuance, containing all the real derivation logic (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE session classification, lightweight-token detection, grant lookup) — is executed by no test in this diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI interface with no default implementation, making every grant factory compiled against the previous interface binary-incompatible. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates all registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances and calls gtf.getShortcut(); a deployment carrying a pre-compiled extension grant throws AbstractMethodError at that call and the server fails to start after upgrading — a hard boot failure with no default method, migration note, or documented shortcut contract for existing grant authors.

This is a binary-incompatible change for any pre-compiled third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations (compiled against the old interface). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The getShortcut() javadoc contracts for 'usually like 3-letters' shortcuts while DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-rejects any encoded context whose length is not exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) with IllegalArgumentException. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff deletes the public Context(Context) copy constructor instead of extending it to propagate the new grantType field alongside the thirteen fields it already copies, removing SPI surface not required by the encoding feature. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor's rawTokenId null check validates the wrong variable — it calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") a second time instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId passes the guard that was written specifically to reject it, and encodeTokenId then string-concatenates it, silently minting a token id ending in the literal text 'null' (e.g. 'onrtna:null') which round-trips through getTokenContextFromTokenId as rawTokenId "null" instead of failing fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getShortcut() is added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory as a non-default abstract method, so every existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation compiled against the previous interface no longer satisfies the contract. When DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates grant factories at startup and calls gtf.getShortcut(), a deployment containing any pre-upgrade custom grant JAR throws AbstractMethodError and the server fails to start — hard-breaking exactly the third-party grants that the factory's own 'Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' lazy paths claim to tolerate; a default method would have avoided the break.

Any existing factory implementation compiled against the previous interface will be binary-incompatible and, if loaded, will throw `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates `OAuth2GrantType` factories and calls `gtf.getShortcut()` unconditionally. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] encodeTokenId concatenates factory.getShortcut() with no length validation while getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-rejects any encoded context whose length != 6, and the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut javadoc explicitly blesses '3-letters' shortcuts. A third-party grant following the interface javadoc with a 3-char shortcut mints access tokens whose ids its own framework decoder throws IllegalArgumentException on ('Expected length of 6'), a write/read format drift invisible to every test because all in-tree shortcuts happen to be 2 chars.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-codes the token-id context format to 6 chars in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId (it throws if encodedContext.length() != 6), implying a 2+2+2 scheme. But encodeTokenId blindly concatenates sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort (no length check) from DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType, which is ultimately sourced from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut(). The new javadoc for getShortcut() explicitly mentions “usually like 3-letters shortcut”, so a 3-char shortcut would produce a 7-char context and then the framework’s own decoder would throw IllegalArgumentException (“Expected length of 6”). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'pg' shortcut is registered for the UMA grant, but no code path in the UMA permission flow ever sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE on its client session context — PermissionGrantType builds its token response directly through tokenManager.responseBuilder rather than OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, and the diff wires none of its sites. Every UMA-ticket access token encodes grant 'na' (or a stale 'grant_type' note left on a reused client session by an earlier grant), so 'pg' is dead vocabulary that is never emitted and UMA tokens are indistinguishable from legacy pre-upgrade tokens to any consumer decoding the id.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `context.grantType` (read from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`) and centrally sets `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType())` inside `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)`. Whether the UMA/Permission grant “builds its token response directly through tokenManager.responseBuilder rather than OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse” is not shown in this diff (no `PermissionGrantType` code is included), so the claim that “no code path in the UMA permission flow ever sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE” and that all UMA tokens will encode `na` cannot be verified from the provided changes and may be false if UMA uses the base helper.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The public copy constructor Context(Context) is deleted from the OAuth2GrantType extension surface, a binary-incompatible removal from the same SPI this framework extends. Any extension grant that clones a Context via 'new Context(other)' — the pattern the constructor existed to support — dies with NoSuchMethodError after upgrade, with no deprecation cycle; source-level implementers get an unexplained compile break alongside the new getShortcut() requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the public copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (it is present in the deleted hunk and no longer exists after the change). Since this class is in `server-spi-private` and used by grant implementations, that is a binary-incompatible API removal: any existing extension compiled against the old SPI that calls `new Context(otherContext)` would fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError` after upgrade. The diff also adds a new abstract SPI method `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()`, which further confirms the SPI surface is being changed incompatibly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Grant-type wiring covers only StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient; the sibling external-to-internal exchange provider mints OIDC access tokens through the same TokenManager.initToken with nobody setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE. Access tokens minted via external token exchange encode grant 'na' instead of the registered 'te' shortcut, so the framework's grant data is wrong for that entire flow and a decoding consumer cannot tell externally-exchanged tokens from legacy ones.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient now sets clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE). The finding’s claim about a “sibling external-to-internal exchange provider” minting tokens via TokenManager.initToken without setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE cannot be verified from this diff because no such provider/class or code path is included here. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Every access token's public jti claim (and event detail Details.TOKEN_ID) changes from a bare UUID to a fixed-width 'xxxyyyzz:uuid' encoding with no version marker, no config to disable it, and zero production consumers of the decode half (getTokenContextFromTokenId is called only by the unit test). Downstream systems that treated jti/TOKEN_ID as UUIDs — an assumption Keycloak's own codebase demonstrably held, since the diff must rewrite four isUUID() matchers in AssertEvents — break silently on upgrade, and operators take that compat risk immediately for a capability nothing reads until a later PR; the rigid positional format also means any future vocabulary change is a hard decode failure rather than a graceful UNKNOWN fallback.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change access token IDs from a bare generated UUID to a fixed-format prefixed encoding: TokenManager.initToken() now builds an AccessTokenContext and sets token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)), where encodeTokenId() returns 6 chars + ':' + raw UUID (e.g. "onrtcc:uuid"). This is reflected by tests needing updates in AssertEvents from isUUID() to isAccessTokenId(...), showing Keycloak itself previously assumed UUID format. The new format has no explicit version marker and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException for unknown shortcuts/lengths rather than gracefully mapping to UNKNOWN (except for the legacy no-colon case), and there is no configuration shown to keep the old UUID-only behavior. These are concrete compatibility/upgrade-risk concerns grounded in the diff, even if not a direct functional defect within this PR alone. The claim that there are 'zero production consumers' of getTokenContextFromTokenId cannot be fully verified from this diff alone, though within the shown changes it’s only exercised by the new unit test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Context eagerly captures grantType as formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE) in the constructor while the adjacent setFormParams mutator replaces formParams without recomputing it, so the two fields can disagree. Any grant implementation that swaps form params after construction — the mutator's entire purpose — mints tokens whose encoded grant type reflects the pre-swap params while context.getFormParams() reports the new ones, producing a silently wrong jti with no inconsistency signal.

adjudication.rationale: In OAuth2GrantType.Context, the new field `grantType` is initialized once in the constructor from `formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE)`, but the existing mutator `setFormParams(...)` updates the `formParams` field without recomputing `grantType`. The diff also shows `context.getGrantType()` being used to stamp `clientSessionCtx` (`OAuth2GrantTypeBase#createTokenResponse` and others), which then feeds into token-id encoding (`TokenManager#initToken` via `TokenContextEncoderProvider`). Therefore, if any code calls `setFormParams` after construction, `context.getFormParams()` and `context.getGrantType()` can disagree and tokens can be minted with a grant type derived from stale params, with no inconsistency check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId never verifies the encoded grant type: it slices the wrong characters (items[0].substring(3,5) instead of the grant shortcut at chars 4-5, i.e. substring(4,6)) and inverts the comparison by returning false when the slice EQUALS the expected shortcut. adjudication.rationale: In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the matcher logic is incorrect: it extracts `items[0].substring(3, 5)` even though the encoded token prefix is 6 chars (`sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2)`), so the grant shortcut should be `substring(4, 6)`. It also inverts the check by returning `false` when the extracted slice *equals* `expectedGrantShortcut`, meaning a correctly encoded token would fail while mismatches pass. Additionally, `substring(3,5)` can throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` for short prefixes instead of returning `false`. This directly affects the rewritten assertions that rely on this matcher.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor's null-guard intended for rawTokenId actually checks grantType a second time (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") at line 71), so rawTokenId is never validated despite the guard's message. A null rawTokenId passes construction and encodeTokenId emits a jti ending in ':null' — the fail-fast contract the error message advertises does not exist, and any caller relying on the constructor's non-null guarantee silently gets corrupted token IDs instead of an NPE at the construction site.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null-check mistakenly calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`, constructor). This means `rawTokenId` is never validated and can be null despite the guard message. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getShortcut() is added to the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI as an abstract method with no default implementation, and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls gtf.getShortcut() on every registered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory during Keycloak startup (factory lines ~69-74). Any operator with a custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory deployed as a JAR compiled against the previous interface gets AbstractMethodError during server startup (or an NPE from ConcurrentHashMap.put if a factory returns a null shortcut), turning a token-ID formatting feature into an unbootable server instead of a degraded feature; a default method returning the id-derived or UNKNOWN shortcut would preserve boot.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, startup code iterates all registered `OAuth2GrantType` factories, casts to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` and then `ConcurrentHashMap.put(grantShortcut, grantName)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] initToken unconditionally rewrites every access token's jti from a plain UUID to a prefixed form (e.g. 'onrtac:<uuid>') via the default TokenContextEncoderProvider, with no feature flag, profile gate, or realm/client option to disable the new format. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Constants.GRANT_TYPE is set only on the exchangeClientToOIDCClient path, so access tokens minted on the sibling user-token exchange path (subject_token=JWT, e.g. exchangeOIDCtoOIDC in the same class) are created with the attribute unset and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider encodes grant type 'na' for them.
